h: Making a splash and making a day of it
p: A little preparation goes a long way. Pack swimwear, a towel each, flip-flops for walking around the poolside and a change of warm clothes. Goggles help anyone who doesn't like water in their eyes, and a waterproof phone pouch is handy if you want photos. Lockers are available, so you can stash valuables safely and get on with the fun.

Book your session in advance, especially at weekends and in the school holidays, when the most popular times fill up fast. Check the height restrictions on the slides before you arrive, so everyone knows what they can try and nobody's disappointed at the top of the steps.

How long to allow? Your session will set the pace, but it's worth arriving a little early to get changed and make the most of your time in the water. Little ones will need breaks, so build in time to warm up and grab a snack.
It's right in the city centre, so you can walk to plenty of cafés and restaurants afterwards rather than having to drive somewhere for food.

Coventry has plenty to fill the rest of your day. The Coventry Transport Museum is a must for anyone who loves cars, bikes and buses, celebrating the city's long role in British motoring and cycling. The Herbert Art Gallery and Museum is close by, with exhibitions on the city's history and art. Don't miss the statue of Lady Godiva in Broadgate, the city's most famous legend. And for something different, FarGo Village has independent shops, street food and a creative vibe that's a lot of fun to wander round.
